title: agent-workflow: GitHub Actions (Layer 3 + 4)
description:
Build the GitHub Actions that automate review, enforce quality gates, and orchestrate the merge flow.

## What
- PR review workflow: trigger 3 reviewers via claude -p on PR open/sync
- Orchestrator status check: blocker evaluation, re-review assessment, cycle cap
- Guardrail checks (5): scope enforcement, test ratio, dependency changes, API surface changes, commit messages
- Workflow configuration (.github/agent-workflow/config.yaml)
- Issue templates (task.yml, review-finding.yml)

## Why
This is what makes the workflow enforced rather than advisory. Without Actions, the skills are just suggestions that agents can ignore.

## Reference
See history/agent-workflow-design.md, Layers 3-5.

title: Write PR review workflow
description:
Write the PR review GitHub Action that triggers three reviewer agents on PR events.

## File
`workflow/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`

## What
- Trigger: PR opened or synchronized (new commits pushed)
- Parse `fixes #N` from PR description to determine parent issue
- Run 3 reviewer skills in parallel via `claude -p`:
  - reviewer-correctness
  - reviewer-tests
  - reviewer-architecture
- Each reviewer creates child issues under #N with severity labels
- Blocking findings are set as blocking #N via GitHub dependency API

## Implementation
- Use `claude-code-action` or direct `claude -p` invocation
- Pass PR diff and codebase context to each reviewer
- Reviewers need the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret
- Each reviewer runs as a separate job for parallelism

## Reference
- Design doc: PR Review Workflow section (Layer 3)
- Reviewer skills (devcontainer-template-tcu.5)

title: Write orchestrator status check
description:
Write the orchestrator status check — the brain that gates PR merges.

## File
`workflow/.github/workflows/orchestrator-check.yml`

## What
- Trigger: issue events (opened, closed, labeled) and PR pushes
- Parse `fixes #N` from PR description
- Check if #N has any open child issues with `blocking` label
- If blockers exist: report failing status check (PR can't merge)
- If no blockers + new "all clear": run lightweight `claude -p` to assess re-review need
- If re-review warranted + under cycle cap (default 3): trigger pr-review.yml again
- If no re-review needed or cap reached: report passing check
- Report results via GitHub Check Run API

## Key logic
- Cycle cap is configurable via .github/agent-workflow/config.yaml
- Re-review assessment prompt needs to be carefully tuned (see design doc Open Question #3)
- When cap reached, report `action_required` for human review

## Reference
- Design doc: Orchestrator Status Check section (Layer 3)

title: Write scope enforcement guardrail
description:
Write the scope enforcement guardrail check.

## File
`workflow/.github/workflows/guardrail-scope.yml`

## What
- Trigger: PR opened or synchronized
- Compare files changed in PR against files listed in the linked issue body
- Parse `fixes #N` → read issue #N body → extract file paths mentioned
- Diff against actual files changed in PR
- If extra files changed: report `action_required` with annotations on unexpected files
- Check for non-stale PR approval — if approved, report `success` despite violations
- Report via GitHub Check Run API with file-level annotations

## Override mechanism
Query PR reviews, check if latest approval's commit_id matches HEAD. If so, violations are accepted.

## Reference
- Design doc: Scope Enforcement (Layer 4), Override Mechanism (Layer 3)

title: Write test-to-code ratio guardrail
description:

- Test files identified by naming convention (*test*, *spec*, __tests__/)
- Configurable threshold from config.yaml (default: 0.5)
- Below threshold: report `action_required`
- Above threshold: report `success`
- Check for non-stale PR approval override

## Reference
- Design doc: Test-to-Code Ratio (Layer 4)

title: Write API surface change guardrail
description:

title: agent-workflow: Setup & Installation
description:
Build the distribution and setup layer — how users adopt the workflow in their projects.

## What
- setup.sh: configure branch protection on main via gh api, set required status checks, enable auto-merge. Idempotent.
- install.sh: curl-able installer that copies workflow files into an existing project. Merges .claude/settings.json, appends to CLAUDE.md, writes new files, warns on conflicts.
- README.md: philosophy, quick start, what you get, configuration reference, how it works.

## Why
The workflow is only useful if people can actually adopt it. The installer must handle existing projects gracefully (no overwrites, merge where possible).

title: Write setup.sh (branch protection)
description:
Write the setup.sh script that configures GitHub branch protection and required checks.

## File
`workflow/setup.sh` (at repo root, not inside workflow/)

Actually: `setup.sh` at repo root — it's run once by the user after installing.

## What
- Configure branch protection on main via `gh api`:
  - Require PRs (no direct pushes)
  - Require status checks to pass before merge
  - Required checks: orchestrator-check, all enabled guardrails
  - Enable auto-merge
- Idempotent — safe to re-run (updates existing settings)
- Requires `gh` CLI authenticated with admin access

## Implementation
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Configure branch protection for agent-workflow
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection \
  --method PUT \
  --field required_status_checks='{"strict":true,"contexts":["orchestrator-check","guardrail/scope-enforcement",...]}'  \
  --field enforce_admins=false \
  --field required_pull_request_reviews=null \
  ...
```

## Reference
- Design doc: Layer 1 (Enforcement)

title: Write install.sh (curl installer)
description:
Write the install.sh script — the curl-able installer that adds the workflow to any project.

## File
`install.sh` at repo root

## What
Users run: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdelfino/agent-workflow/main/install.sh | bash`

The script:
1. Downloads the workflow/ directory contents from GitHub
2. Copies files into the current project:
   - `.claude/skills/*` — safe copy (new directories)
   - `.claude/commands/*` — safe copy (new files)
   - `.github/workflows/*` — safe copy (new files, warn if exists)
   - `.github/agent-workflow/config.yaml` — write if absent, warn if exists
   - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*` — safe copy
   - `AGENTS.md` — write if absent, warn if exists
3. Merges config files:
   - `.claude/settings.json` — merge permissions array (add gh:* and git:* if not present), merge hooks
   - `CLAUDE.md` — append workflow section if not already present (detect by marker comment)
   - `.gitignore` — no changes needed (no beads)
4. Reports what was installed, what was skipped, what needs manual attention

## Key design decisions
- No dependencies (pure bash + curl + jq for JSON merge)
- Never overwrites existing files without asking
- Merge strategy for settings.json: read existing, add missing permissions, write back
- CLAUDE.md append uses a marker: `<!-- agent-workflow -->` to detect existing install
- All downloads from raw.githubusercontent.com/jdelfino/agent-workflow/main/workflow/

## Edge cases
- Project has no .claude/ directory → create it
- Project has .claude/settings.json with existing permissions → merge, don't replace
- Project has no CLAUDE.md → create from template
- .github/workflows/ already has files with same names → warn, don't overwrite

title: Write coordinator/work skill
description:
Write the coordinator/work skill — the recursive /work #N entry point.

## File
`workflow/.claude/skills/coordinator/SKILL.md`

## What
This is the biggest rewrite. The current coordinator (template/.claude/skills/coordinator/SKILL.md) uses beads and a simpler branching model. The new version implements the hierarchical branching from the design doc.

### /work #N behavior:
1. Fetch issue #N via `gh issue view N --json`
2. Find parent issue (if any) → determine base branch
   - Has parent P → base is `feat/{P}-{slug}`
   - No parent → base is `main`
3. Determine if #N is a leaf (no sub-issues) or non-leaf (has sub-issues)
4. **If leaf:**
   - Check out the PARENT's branch (do NOT create a new branch for leaves)
   - Rebase on base branch if behind
   - Spawn implementer subagent for the work
   - Commits land directly on the parent's branch
5. **If non-leaf:**
   - Check if branch `feat/{N}-{slug}` already exists
     - If yes: check it out, rebase on base branch if behind
     - If no: create branch off base
   - Create/update PR targeting base branch with `fixes #N`
   - Work through unblocked children (query for sub-issues with no open blocked-by deps)
6. Handle review findings: on re-run, open blocking children are treated the same as regular children — /work is /cleanup

### Key design points:
- /work is both "implement" and "cleanup" — no separate command
- Rebase before starting work (no /merge needed)
- Branch hierarchy mirrors issue hierarchy
- PR targets parent's branch, not main (unless top-level)
- **Leaf tasks commit directly to parent's branch** — no sub-branch, no sub-PR
- **Non-leaf issues get their own branch and PR**
- For non-leaf, orchestrate children sequentially (work through unblocked ones)

### Triage logic (from current coordinator, adapted):
- If given a description instead of issue number: create issue first, then proceed
- If branch already exists: check it out and rebase (supports re-runs for cleanup)

### GitHub API operations (see tcu.9 for exact API calls):
- Query sub-issues of #N
- Query blocked-by dependencies to find unblocked children
- Create/edit issues for review findings

## Reference
- Current: template/.claude/skills/coordinator/SKILL.md
- Design doc: Implementation Skill section, Hierarchical Branching section
- tcu.9: GitHub GraphQL API reference for sub-issues and dependencies
- End-to-end workflow examples in design doc

## What
Rewrite the current reviewer skills to output GitHub Issues instead of beads findings.

### Approach: template one, adapt the others
The three reviewers share identical scaffolding:
1. Write the common reviewer framework FIRST:
   - Parse `fixes #N` from PR description
   - Review the diff
   - For each finding: create a GitHub child issue with severity label
   - For blocking findings: set blocking relationship via GraphQL API
2. Then adapt the checklist section for each reviewer's domain

### Common output format (all three):
```bash
gh issue create \
  --title "Finding: <description>" \
  --label "severity:<blocking|should-fix|suggestion>" \
  --body "<detailed description with file refs and line numbers>"
# Then set as sub-issue of #N and blocking relationship via GraphQL (see tcu.9)
```

### Review concerns per skill:
- **Correctness:** bugs, nil/null dereference, race conditions, error handling, security (injection, XSS, secrets), API contract mismatches
- **Tests:** meaningful coverage, edge cases, integration tests, mock vs real balance, test accuracy
- **Architecture:** duplication across codebase (not just diff), pattern divergence, unnecessary complexity, missing shared types/utilities

### Invocation:
- Run via `claude -p` in GitHub Actions (Layer 3)
- Also invocable locally by coordinator skill
- Input: PR diff + codebase context

### GitHub API operations (see tcu.9):
- Create sub-issue under parent
- Set blocking relationship for critical findings

title: Document GitHub GraphQL API for sub-issues and dependencies
description:
Research and document the exact GitHub CLI / GraphQL API calls for sub-issues and dependency management.

## File
Add to `workflow/AGENTS.md` (or a separate reference doc linked from AGENTS.md)

## What
The gh CLI may not natively support sub-issue creation or blocked-by relationships. Research the current state and document:

### Required operations:
1. **Create sub-issue** (set parent-child relationship)
   - Does `gh issue create --parent N` work? If not, what's the GraphQL mutation?
   - Query: list sub-issues of a parent

2. **Add blocked-by / blocking relationship**
   - GraphQL mutation to set blocked-by between two issues
   - Query: list issues blocked by a given issue
   - Query: check if an issue has any open blocking children

3. **Query unblocked children**
   - Find sub-issues of #N that have no open blocked-by dependencies
   - This is needed by /work to know which children to work on next

### Deliverable:
A reference section (in AGENTS.md or linked doc) with exact `gh api graphql` commands for each operation. Example:
```bash
# Create sub-issue
gh api graphql -f query='mutation { ... }'

# Add blocked-by relationship
gh api graphql -f query='mutation { ... }'

# List unblocked children of #N
gh api graphql -f query='query { ... }'
```

## Why
Multiple tasks (planner, coordinator, reviewers) need these API calls. Documenting them once prevents three sessions doing the same research and arriving at incompatible approaches.

## Dependencies
- Should be one of the first tasks completed in Epic 2
- tcu.2 (planner), tcu.3 (coordinator), tcu.5 (reviewers) all reference this
